problem: Visual captioning models assume a well-captured single image, and fail when the viewpoint is poor or objects are occluded. Prior embodied scene description work only uses pretrained captioners, has no in-domain dataset, and navigates to enlarge explored area rather than to improve captions.
motivation: Real-world images are often taken from suboptimal viewpoints, so a captioner should actively move to gather information and reduce visual ambiguity. There is no benchmark with annotated good viewpoints and paragraph descriptions to study navigation entangled with captioning.
key_idea: Introduce the Embodied Captioning task and the ET-Cap dataset, and solve it with a cascade of a history-aware navigator (imitation learning toward annotated good viewpoints) and a trajectory-aware captioner that cross-attends over all trajectory images.
insight: Merging visual information at the trajectory level matters more than using only the end view (oracle captioning: trajectory-level cross-attention r4 CIDEr 39.49 vs single-view r2 29.34), and the region-level and trajectory-level attention are complementary (r5 42.10). Historical vision and action information improve navigation, and better navigation gives better captions. An exploratory 'joint' oracle experiment that picks the best partial trajectory by CIDEr improves CIDEr from 40.83 to 66.38, suggesting captioning-guided navigation has large headroom.
method: ET-Cap dataset: 10K Kubric scenes (ShapeNet + GSO assets, physics-based placement of 3-7 objects around a base furniture), 8x8x4 m grid with 0.4 m cells, three human paragraphs per scene, and human-selected good viewpoints among 20 candidates.

Ground-truth trajectories: Dijkstra shortest path from random start to an annotated good viewpoint, step length up to 1.6 m, camera always rotated to look at the scene center; 72,594 trajectories in total.

Action space: five action types (forward-backward, left-right, up-down moves, heading rotation, elevation rotation), each a direction classification plus a magnitude regression; the agent stops when all types output 'stop'.

History-aware Navigator: ResNet backbone, a Region Encoder (self-attention over regions), a Historical Vision Encoder (causal attention over the same region across time), and a Historical Action-informed Decoder (causal transformer over mean-pooled visual features concatenated with the embedded previous action). Trained with CE + 2.0 x L1.

Trajectory-aware Captioner: DETR-pretrained ResNet backbone (in-domain detector trained on 4,398 extra scenes), Region Encoder, and a Bi-CrossAttention Decoder that cross-attends over region-level pooled features (mean over time) and trajectory-level pooled features (mean over regions).
Cascade inference: the navigator and captioner are trained separately on ground-truth trajectories; at test time the navigator produces a trajectory and the captioner describes it.

Metrics: captioning metrics multiplied by a length penalty r^l = L_gt/max(L_gt, L_pred); navigation is measured by NE (Manhattan distance to good viewpoints), CLIP-based Image Similarity (IS) and Segmentation Similarity (SS), each averaged over the trajectory.

setting.backbone: ResNet + Transformer navigator and captioner (trained from scratch; captioner backbone initialized from an in-domain DETR)
setting.training_data: ET-Cap train split: 8,324 scenes, 24,972 captions, 60,474 GT trajectories; plus 4,398 extra scenes (87,960 images) for DETR detector pretraining
setting.observation: monocular RGB image with restricted field of view, no localization information
setting.action_space: continuous-magnitude actions in a 3D grid world: 5 action types, each with direction classification and magnitude regression (up to 1.6 m, rotations in degrees)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT locations used only to generate training trajectories)

The NE_l, IS_l and SS_l keys are the length-penalized variants (NE^l etc.). Per-subset (Common / Novel Instance / Novel Category) results are in Tab. 4 and are not listed above.
results: CaBOT's best navigator (with visual and action history) plus the trajectory-aware captioner reaches CIDEr 40.83 and CIDEr^l 34.88, well above the rule-based navigator (CIDEr 33.90, CIDEr^l 15.80) and the no-history navigator (CIDEr 40.59). With oracle trajectories the captioner reaches CIDEr 45.24, still far below human performance (96.72), and unseen object categories cause a large captioning drop (CIDEr^l 26.63 vs 37.60 on Common).
limitations: Scenes are synthetic and simple (3-7 objects, few obstacles), so transfer to real environments is untested.
The navigator is trained only by imitation on GT trajectories and fails when it reaches a bad viewpoint with no visible instances (unseen states); RL or data augmentation is left to future work.
Navigation and captioning are trained separately and cascaded, so the captioner cannot guide exploration; the joint variant is only an oracle analysis.
